summary: Dedicated customer requesting explicit reserved throughput guarantees for a specific API route (/v1/chat/completions) and clarification on how this interacts with priority lanes / throttling
description:
Issue summary
HelioPay (Dedicated, us-east) is requesting an explicit reserved throughput guarantee for a specific route used by their production app: POST /v1/chat/completions (model pinned to rw-llama-70b-instruct, streaming enabled). They want contract-grade language and/or a numeric commitment (RPS and/or tokens/sec) that is guaranteed for that route even during platform overload, and they want to understand how the new hot-route capacity protection / priority lanes affect Dedicated behavior.

Customer context
- HelioPay has a Dedicated GPU pool in us-east.
- Traffic pattern: one dominant route (/v1/chat/completions) plus a smaller embeddings route.
- They run bursty traffic (billing cycles / batch processing) and they have client retries enabled (exponential backoff).
- They observed elevated 429s during a recent us-east capacity dip and are concerned the platform is "throttling their paid reserved capacity".

Customer request (verbatim paraphrase)
1) "We need a reserved throughput number for /v1/chat/completions that you guarantee (e.g., X requests/sec or Y tokens/sec) and what happens if we exceed it."
2) "If you enable enterprise priority lanes / hot-route protection, do we get put behind other customers?"
3) "We need a written statement we can share internally that Dedicated capacity is not subject to shared-fleet throttling." 

Impact
- Business / contract risk: customer is asking for explicit guarantees; they may block expansion if we cannot provide them.
- Support risk: confusion between rate limiting (gateway) vs capacity admission (router/runtime) vs Dedicated isolation.

Environment
- prod, us-east
- Dedicated pool: HelioPay-dedicated-us-east (internal name redacted in customer comms)
- Route: POST /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)
- Model: rw-llama-70b-instruct (pinned)

What we know so far
- The recent 429s appear correlated with protective admission control during the us-east dip (router shed + gateway rate limit), but we need to confirm whether the 429s were coming from gateway (rate limit / quota) or router (over-capacity / lane admission).
- Dedicated today provides capacity isolation at the pool level, but we do not offer per-route reserved scheduling guarantees (and we do not want to commit to an unqualified tokens/sec number without workload constraints).

Asks / next steps
- Escalate to Product (Lauren Bishop) for contract/positioning alignment: what can we commit to for Dedicated (pool-level vs route-level) and what language should Support/CS use.
- Escalate to SRE (Sean Gallagher) for policy alignment: confirm whether any hot-route protection policies can/should apply to Dedicated pools, and what the documented behavior is.
- Provide customer-ready response: (a) what Dedicated guarantees today, (b) what we can measure and share (observed throughput under test), (c) mitigation plan (load test + tuning + client retry guidance).

Internal notes / hypotheses
- If any shared control-plane limits are being applied (tenant-level safety caps) they may still produce 429s even for Dedicated pools; we need to confirm intended behavior and document exceptions/overrides.
- The customer’s burst + retry strategy could be amplifying queue pressure and triggering shedding; we should give explicit Retry-After guidance and recommended retry caps.

Links
- Prior related tickets: SUP-24118 (elevated 429s during burst), SUP-24133 (inconsistent throttling across regions)
- Program: Hot-route capacity protection (priority lanes, standardized 429 semantics)
- Runbook: overload throttling and priority routing response
comments: 2025-01-29 09:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Opened per CS escalation. HelioPay wants a route-specific throughput guarantee for /v1/chat/completions. Routing to Liam (TAM) for customer-facing response and coordinating with Lauren (PM Dedicated) + Sean (SRE sponsor).

2025-01-29 10:03 PT — Liam O'Rourke (Enterprise comms/TAM) — Acknowledged. Scheduling quick sync with HelioPay Eng today. Requesting from SRE: confirm whether any gateway rate-limit policies apply to Dedicated pools + what headers/reason codes they should see on 429s.

2025-01-29 11:20 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Quick check: during INC-2025-01-18-us-east-capacity-dip we enabled protective admission controls on shared fleet. Dedicated pools should not be routed through shared enterprise lane logic, but gateway safety caps may still apply if configured at tenant-level. Action: verify the 429 reason codes in logs for HelioPay (need request IDs).

2025-01-29 13:45 PT — Liam O'Rourke (TAM) — Customer call notes: they want 'at least 60 RPS' for chat completions or equivalent tokens/sec. They are willing to provide their prompt+max_tokens distribution for sizing, but they want something in writing. They reported seeing Retry-After sometimes missing; asked if that’s expected.

2025-01-29 14:10 PT — Aisha Bello (SRE) — Retry-After missing is likely older gateway behavior; new standardized throttling responses are landing with reason codes + Retry-After (see redwood/pr-18463). For now, router-shed 429s may not include Retry-After consistently; we should not promise otherwise until rollout completes.

2025-01-30 09:02 PT — Lauren Bishop (Product, Dedicated) — Dedicated commitment is currently expressed as reserved GPU capacity + pool isolation and SLA for availability/latency, not per-route tokens/sec. We can offer a documented 'capacity planning' process: run a perf test with their workload, publish an observed steady-state throughput range, and set an operational alert threshold. For contract language, route-specific guarantees need Legal + Sales; not something Support can commit to. Please position route-level as 'best-effort within reserved pool' until we have per-route lane reservation for Dedicated.

2025-01-30 10:18 PT — Sean Gallagher (SRE sponsor) — Aligning on policy: hot-route capacity protection is designed primarily to protect shared hosted fleet and enterprise lanes. Dedicated pools can still have safety mechanisms (to prevent a single tenant from self-DOS via retry storms) but those should be transparent and documented. We should commit to: (1) Dedicated traffic does not compete with self-serve fleet capacity, (2) any throttling in Dedicated is due to tenant-local limits/safety/backpressure, and (3) we provide clear reason codes + Retry-After as we roll out standardization.

2025-01-31 15:40 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Sent HelioPay a request for 5 example request IDs from the 429 window + their typical prompt length and max_tokens distribution. Also asked whether they use parallel retries and if they cap concurrency client-side.

2025-02-03 11:27 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Found sample in logs from customer-provided request IDs: majority 429s were 'over_capacity' from router admission due to queue depth spikes inside the dedicated pool (not shared fleet). A smaller set were gateway 'rate_limit' tied to a conservative per-tenant burst cap. Recommendation: raise burst cap for HelioPay route and enable standardized 429 payloads + Retry-After once flag is available for dedicated path.

2025-02-04 09:55 PT — Liam O'Rourke (TAM) — Drafted customer response for review: we can’t provide an unconditional RPS/tokens/sec guarantee for a single route today; Dedicated guarantees reserved GPU pool isolation and we will jointly size for target throughput using their workload. Also clarified that enterprise lanes are a shared-fleet protection feature and do not deprioritize their Dedicated pool. Waiting for Lauren to approve wording.

2025-02-04 12:30 PT — Lauren Bishop (PM) — Approved with edits: be explicit that any numeric throughput is dependent on model, prompt length, max_tokens, and concurrency; offer a written 'Throughput Sizing Note' (not SLA) after we run a load test. Also add note that we are standardizing 429 semantics including Retry-After and reason codes, with rollout tracking under ENG-4826.

2025-02-05 16:05 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Customer accepted the approach (sizing note + burst cap adjustment) and asked for ETA for standardized Retry-After on 429s. We pointed to upcoming rollout and committed to keep them updated via email thread.

2025-02-06 09:10 PT — Liam O'Rourke (TAM) — Closing as resolved on Support side. Follow-ups filed: PM-611 for Dedicated customer-facing throttling/guarantee language; and internal action with SRE to adjust HelioPay burst cap and ensure 429 reason codes are visible in their logs/Console.
resolution:
Resolved with customer-facing clarification and an agreed plan:
- Dedicated guarantees reserved GPU pool isolation and does not compete with self-serve/shared fleet capacity.
- We cannot provide an unconditional per-route throughput guarantee (RPS/tokens/sec) for /v1/chat/completions today; route-level throughput depends on workload characteristics.
- We will produce a written 'Throughput Sizing Note' after running a joint load test using HelioPay’s prompt/max_tokens distribution, and we will tune tenant-local burst caps to reduce unnecessary 429s.
- We aligned internally that hot-route enterprise priority lanes are a shared-fleet protection mechanism and should not deprioritize Dedicated pools; any throttling in Dedicated should be tenant-local and transparent via standardized 429 reason codes and Retry-After as rollout completes.

Follow-ups tracked via PM-611 and ENG-4826; SRE to implement burst-cap adjustment and verify reason code visibility.

Product: finalize Dedicated docs language for throttling vs reserved capacity (PM-611) and provide a standard customer template for TAMs/Support
Eng: ensure standardized 429 payload + Retry-After coverage for router-shed paths in Dedicated rollout (ENG-4826)
